_provenance.notes: Alaska sport fishing is one of the state's largest economic sectors — generating over $2B in annual economic impact. The Kenai River is the single most valuable sport fishery in the world (by angler-days × expenditure per day). Alaska has 3,000+ sport fishing guide businesses. The in-season conflict between sport fishers (rods) and commercial fishers (nets) in Upper Cook Inlet is one of the most politically charged ongoing fisheries allocation disputes in Alaska. Kenai River late-run sockeye personal use dipnet fishery draws 50,000+ Alaskans annually — a cultural phenomenon unique to Alaska.

dipnet_fishery.description: Kenai River personal use dipnet — Alaska-resident only, culturally unique
dipnet_fishery.eligibility: Alaska residents ONLY — must be physically present in Alaska 12+ months
dipnet_fishery.notes: The dipnet fishery is the most popular personal use fishery in Alaska. Thousands of families drive from Anchorage to the Kenai mouth, camp on the beach, and use large circular nets in the surf to catch sockeye as they run upstream. A cultural phenomenon with no equivalent anywhere else.

allocation_conflict.description: Cook Inlet commercial vs sport allocation — the most politically contentious ongoing Alaska fisheries issue
allocation_conflict.2018_bof_action: BOF reduced commercial set net allocation in Upper Cook Inlet by ~30%, redirecting salmon to sport and personal use sectors
allocation_conflict.litigation: Multiple commercial fishermen filed legal challenges (Dunleavy v. ADF&G) — BOF authority upheld
